questions.question: Define an element and a compound and give two examples of each.
questions.expected_answer: An element is a pure substance made of only one kind of atom that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means; examples iron, oxygen, carbon, gold. A compound is a substance made of two or more elements chemically joined; examples water (hydrogen and oxygen), carbon dioxide, table salt (sodium and chlorine).

questions.question: Describe how Mendeleev arranged his Periodic Table and explain why the discovery of gallium was important.
questions.expected_answer: In 1869 Mendeleev arranged the 63 known elements in order of increasing atomic mass, starting a new row when properties began to repeat, so that elements with similar properties were in the same column. He sometimes swapped elements to keep families together and left gaps for undiscovered elements, predicting their properties. Gallium, discovered in 1875, had properties that closely matched his prediction for eka-aluminium, which showed that his table revealed a real pattern and could make correct predictions; scandium and germanium also matched.

questions.question: Describe where metals, non-metals and semi-metals are found on the modern Periodic Table and give two examples of each.
questions.expected_answer: Metals are on the left and in the centre (about three quarters of the elements); examples sodium, iron, copper, gold. Non-metals are on the far right, plus hydrogen at the top left; examples oxygen, nitrogen, carbon, helium, chlorine. Semi-metals lie along the staircase (zigzag line) between them and have some properties of each; examples boron, silicon, germanium, arsenic.
